# True Widescreen

This built-in package selects native 16:9 and widens the stage visibility cone
using the actual viewport width. The original 6x6 section map and its geometry
are preserved. Stage sections are not repeated, and the renderer composes each
frame from current geometry instead of retaining old camera views.

The visibility hooks run in native code and the interpreter without modifying
guest code pages. Fighters retain their original camera projection.

**Wider fight framing (experimental)** is enabled by default. Regular battles
can use the extra horizontal view before the camera pulls back. Close-range
framing and the vertical fit stay original; movement speed, collision and the
maximum world-space separation are unchanged. This adjusts the camera's framing
of the fighters, including unlocked characters and custom outfits. The alternate
cinematic camera and modes 6/7 are excluded.

Turn this option off under **True 16:9 Widescreen** in the Mods page to compare
the original fight camera while retaining the wide stages and menus. Restart
the game after changing it.

The native camera variant is generated by `tools/build_fight_camera.py` from
`func_80064E10`. Eight exact MIPS-word and generated-operand guards cover its
horizontal focal calculations. All other generated instructions, continuation
handling and cycle accounting are preserved. The actual GTE focal length and
guest code bytes are unchanged.

Character select and the versus/loading screen have native 16:9 layouts.
The original cabinet background fills the selector, including the game's
black-to-red gradient behind the unlocked roster. Portraits, names and frames
retain their proportions. The versus screen keeps its original background.
The selector roster uses the full width and
its cursor follows each character. The versus image stays wide while the next
stage loads. After confirming a character, the completed selector stays wide
during the CD/upload pause until the next scene starts drawing; it does not
briefly expose the original 4:3 menu.

The main menu also uses native 16:9: the original logo and scrolling lettering
keep their proportions, and the selection bar spans the wider screen. Team
Battle spreads all seven roster columns across the wider canvas, moving each
portrait's border and cursor together. Team slots and prompts anchor to their
respective sides; the original red gradients and animated backdrop remain.
Tekken Force and Team Battle loading also use native 16:9. Their original
lightning background fills the canvas; Force's stage title and portrait, and
Team Battle's fighters, names and remaining teammates keep their proportions.
Loading transitions retain the completed wide image throughout CD waits.

Tekken Force gameplay reveals additional columns from its original scrolling
background tile and palette maps. Only verified map rows can add cells, and
those cells stay outside the original framebuffer. This preserves the original
tile scale, draw order and map wrapping without duplicating visible scenery or
expanding the guest's fixed-size sprite buffers. The background's solid sky
underlay extends to the same width.

Unrecognized menus and movies remain 4:3.

Returning from gameplay keeps the completed wide image throughout the no-draw
menu-loading wait. Menu navigation remains wide when the selection bar is
temporarily absent. New scene drawing, framebuffer uploads and movie/display
changes end gameplay retention immediately.

The retained roster gradient is reconstructed in the widescreen surface even
when it is outside the game's upper-panel clipping area. Its original colors
and draw order are preserved, with no replacement background image.

Disable **True 16:9 Widescreen** in the Mods page to restore exact 4:3.
